turns.text: Why does Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks deserve its own place in the history of artificial intelligence?

Convolutional networks usually treated channels as a fixed stack even though different channels carry different semantic signals. Squeeze-and-Excitation networks asked whether a model could learn to recalibrate those channels for each input.

A squeeze operation summarizes each channel globally, and a small excitation network predicts channel-wise gates. Multiplying those gates back into the feature map lets the network amplify informative channels and suppress weaker ones.

Experts generally regard channel attention as a simple but durable architectural idea, and SE blocks became a common addition to CNN backbones. The work also helped establish attention as a mechanism that could operate beyond sequence models.
As today's systems grow larger, which lessons from Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks still matter, and which limits deserve to be questioned again?
